subject: gas stove indoor air
title: What If You Cooked on a Gas Stove Every Day?

scenes.text: What if you cooked on a gas stove every day? It pollutes even when it's switched off.
Within minutes in a small kitchen with no hood, nitrogen dioxide can pass the US one-hour guideline.
One burner on high, or an oven at three hundred fifty degrees, can push indoor benzene above secondhand smoke levels.
After an oven runs ninety minutes, the gas reaches even the farthest bedroom, and it lingers there for hours.
Outside-vented hoods removed only ten to seventy percent, and cooks use them just a quarter to forty percent of the time.
With the knobs off? Over three quarters of its methane leaks out then. Nationwide, that warms like half a million cars.

description:
What if you cooked on a gas stove every day? Stanford researchers measuring 53 California homes found that without a range hood or good ventilation, nitrogen dioxide can exceed the EPA one-hour guideline within minutes, especially in small kitchens, and more than three-quarters of stove methane leaks while the stove is off (comparable to about 500,000 cars' emissions nationwide).
A 2023 Stanford study found one burner on high or an oven at 350F can raise indoor benzene above secondhand-smoke levels; a later Stanford-led study found NO2 reached distant bedrooms and lingered for hours, with outdoor-vented hoods 10-70% effective.
